variant_decisions.evidence: Qere עָשָׂה֩ is the verb “he made” (Vqp3ms, Strong 6213); ketiv עשר is the numeral “ten” (Acmsa, Strong 6240). ASV “Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold” supplies a finite verb and no number at all; the ketiv would leave the clause verbless and count the ships. “made” distinguishes the qere.

Qere נִשְׁבְּר֥וּ is VNp3cp and ketiv נשברה is VNp3fs, the same Niphal perfect of שָׁבַר with the same feminine plural subject אֳנִיּוֹת, which takes either agreement in Hebrew.
